feedback: D1: You catalogued nine of the ten findings with the right OWASP class and CWE on the core five, and your quoted line for the hardcoded secret 'sankofa-legacy-admin-2019' and the SQLi payload admin' OR '1'='1 at 02:15:31 were spot on. Two real gaps hurt you. The XXE finding (04-import-xxe.xml, SYSTEM file:///etc/passwd via import.php, A05/CWE-611) is missing entirely, and the MD5 entry sits in a summary line with no quoted source line and no salt note. Your access-control trio of path traversal, open redirect and cookie flags was all present, which I credited fully. The decoy is where you lost the most. The real safe construct is the constant-time HS256 verify branch using hash_equals, which is sound at the mechanism level, so the honest verdict is that the tempting hash_equals path is NOT the bug and the real flaws are alg:none and the hardcoded secret. You instead picked the 'attacker was a legitimate user' narrative claim, which is not the decoy the key asks for, so that row scored zero. D2: Your chain runs in time order with verbatim PoCs for SQLi, the XSS beacon to 185.220.101.9:8443, the open redirect and the path read, which is good evidence discipline. The chain is incomplete though, the bulk PII pull is folded into enumeration rather than called out at 02:16:04 as 312 rows, and the parallel XXE file read is absent. On CVSS you scored the SQLi 9.8 with A:H, but an auth bypass does not degrade availability, so the defensible vector is CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N at about 9.1. Your impact section names 312 records but gives no naira, no balance summing into the tens of millions, no BoltCash tie-in and no stated assumptions, which is the single biggest D2 miss. D3: The executive summary is readable and jargon-free, but it ends on '312 records' rather than the customers-and-naira headline a board needs. Your threat model, evidence-linked findings and earliest-break fix (parameterize the login query) were solid. Two things capped you. You state the remediation ordering 'combines CVSS severity with implementation feasibility', and an order anchored to CVSS rather than pure effort-to-risk caps that row at half. Your two detection stopgaps name exact log fields, the username/password POST params and the JWT alg/exp/uid claims, but you gave qualitative 'Moderate/Low' instead of an actual false-positive rate, so quote a percentage next time. D4: Strong work, you answered all four prompts with an owned decision, cited ISC2 Canons 1, 2 and 4 by number as load-bearing, and tied NDPA 2023 Section 40(2) 72-hour regulator notice and 40(3) data-subject notice to the 312 customers, anchored to the 2022 decommission deadline from the evidence. I looked hard for a way to push this into the 70s, and the honest answer is the missing XXE finding, the wrong decoy, the CVSS-anchored remediation order and the absent naira impact are four real gaps that the work does not let me round past. The single most important fix: identify the actual decoy by proving the hash_equals HS256 branch is constant-time and therefore safe, and stop labelling the legitimate-user narrative or alg:none as the decoy.
